_doc: TuRu - the three category sets (Phase G, 2026-09-21). They answer three DIFFERENT questions and
must not be conflated again. tests/categoryStorageModel.test.js enforces every rule below.
categories             WHAT MAY BE ASSIGNED. Handed to the AI extraction model as the list to
choose from (extraction.ts CATEGORY_VALUES) and used as the accept-list
of sanitizeCategory(), which validates the model's ANSWER. A value that
is not here can never enter the catalogue through ingestion.
storageOnlyCategories  WHAT MAY LEGALLY EXIST in activities.category but must never be handed
to a classifier. Union with `categories` = the valid-storage set, which
is what the DB CHECK constraint (supabase/0103) allows.
archiveCategories      COMMITMENT SEMANTICS, an orthogonal overlay. A row holding one of these
is a commitment activity: hidden from the user-facing category options
(constants/filterSchema.js) and blocked from being restored to approved
(shouldArchiveForCommitment, tools/import-tool/server.js).
WHY storageOnlyCategories EXISTS: 'קייטנה' is an intentional TuRu value - it is half of the
commitment/restore gate and two archived production rows hold it - but it was never in
`categories`, so the canonical layer treated it as corruption. Promoting it into `categories`
would have fixed the constraint by telling every AI classifier to start generating camps.
Keeping it storage-only fixes the integrity layer and changes no classifier behaviour.
Contrast 'חוג', which is in BOTH `categories` and `archiveCategories`: a model may assign it and
the record is then auto-archived. That stays exactly as it was.
